reply:
I think you might be thinking of cases where you've *passed a comparator* function. If you've always done `.sort((a, b) => a - b)` or similar, then yes, it sorts numerically.

But try this in your browser console without a comparator:

```javascript
[10, 9, 1].sort()  // returns [1, 10, 9]
```

This really does happen because JavaScript converts all elements to strings and sorts lexicographically. As strings: "1" < "10" < "9".

When you mix strings and numbers, it's the *same* behavior—everything becomes strings. You likely haven't noticed this before if you've consistently been passing a comparator when sorting numbers.
